title: A Jagged Frontier: Evaluating Robustness of Code Agents to Semantics-Preserving Transformations
description: Research evaluating code agent robustness when code undergoes semantics-preserving transformations (e.g., renaming variables, refactoring). Findings show that code agents exhibit a 'jagged frontier' - robust in some areas but fragile in others when facing transformed code that maintains the same functionality.
author: Hasan Najib Mahmud, Shreya Gupta, Isha Chaudhary, Nathaniel Enis, Ravi Mangal, Gagandeep Singh, Corina Pasareanu

title: ComponentBench: Diagnosing Component-Level Failures in Computer-Use Agents
description: New benchmark for diagnosing component-level failures in computer-use agents. Addresses the challenge of identifying which specific components (perception, planning, execution) fail when AI agents attempt computer tasks. Accepted at COLM 2026.
author: Tianchen Guan, Xinlei Lin, Royce Cheng-Yue, Xiangjun Wang, Shuyan Zhou

title: Adversarial Review: Structured Disagreement for Grounded Agentic Code Review
description: Novel approach for AI-powered code review using structured adversarial review processes. The method introduces controlled disagreement between AI reviewers to ground code review feedback and improve reliability. Accepted to ICML 2026 Workshop on DL4C.
author: Eric S. Qiu, Joyce Gill

title: Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling
description: Research demonstrating that looped language models significantly improve compositional tool calling capabilities. Shows that iterative processing enables better tool selection and composition for AI agents.
author: Andrei Cristian Popescu, Haitz Sáez de Ocáriz Borde, Pietro Liò

title: FACET: Preserving Source Intent and Executable State in Terminal Task Synthesis
description: New method for AI terminal task synthesis that preserves both source intent and executable state. Addresses the challenge of maintaining semantic meaning when AI agents automate terminal commands and system operations.
author: Kou Shi, Zun Wang, Qisheng Su, Shiting Huang, Ziao Zhang, Zhen Fang, Qingnan Ren, Jin Liu, Yu Zeng, Yiming Zhao, Lin Chen, Zehui Chen, Feng Zhao

title: Training-Free Inference-Time Self-Reflection and Cost-Bounded Early Stopping for Large Language Models
description: Novel approach for LLM self-reflection during inference without additional training. Introduces cost-bounded early stopping mechanisms to optimize the trade-off between computation time and response quality.
author: Wei Yu, Suxing Liu, Minjie Yu, Jiahao Wang, Zhijian Zheng, Haocheng Deng, Bing Li

title: Metrics That Write Themselves: Evolving an Evaluator from Its Own Blind Spots
description: Novel meta-evaluation approach where metrics evolve and improve based on their own blind spots. Addresses the challenge of automated evaluation systems becoming stale or gaming the metrics they're supposed to measure.
author: Xing Zhang, Yanwei Cui, Guanghui Wang, Zhihao Lin, Peiyang He

title: Eureka: Task-Conditioned Meta-Agent Orchestration for Scientific Discovery
description: New meta-agent orchestration system for AI-driven scientific discovery. Uses task-conditioned approaches to coordinate multiple AI agents for complex research tasks, demonstrating advances in agentic AI for scientific applications.
author: Alizer Wong, Heng Cui, Yi Tan, Xiongchao Zhan, Liang Lin, Yuxiang Guo, Zhaorong Dai, Zixin Zeng, Wenyuan Li

title: DentAgent: Evidence-Centric Multi-Agent Coordination for Multimodal Dental Reasoning
description: Multi-agent system for dental reasoning using evidence-centric coordination. Demonstrates how multiple specialized AI agents can work together for medical imaging analysis and diagnosis in dental healthcare.
author: Zijie Meng, Xiwei Dai, Yixuan Tang, Jin Hao, Yang Feng, Fudong Zhu, Xiaoqiang Liu, Shaosheng Cao, Zuozhu Liu

title: SkillGate: Training In-Policy Skill Selection in Long-Horizon Agents
description: Novel approach for training skill selection in long-horizon AI agents. SkillGate enables agents to select and execute appropriate skills across extended task sequences, addressing a key challenge in agentic AI.
author: Qingyao Li, Wenxiang Jiao, Shuai Shao, Kangning Zhang, Yuan Lu, Yi Guo, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Yong Yu

title: ORBITER: Conflict-Aware Decision-Making for Agentic Last-Mile Delivery
description: New conflict-aware decision-making framework for AI agents in last-mile delivery scenarios. ORBITER handles resource conflicts and optimization challenges in autonomous delivery systems.
author: Mingzhao Li, Chenxi Liu, Yan Zhao, Hao Miao

title: Tuning the Stochastic Machine: A Systems Engineer's Operating Model for Human-AI Engineering
description: Operating model for systems engineers working with human-AI collaborative systems. Provides practical framework for 'tuning the stochastic machine' - managing the probabilistic nature of AI systems in engineering contexts.
author: George Andrikopoulos

title: Grouping the Stochastic Machine: Precision, Not Capability, as the Frontier Metric for AI Systems
description: Argues that precision, not capability, should be the frontier metric for AI systems. Challenges the current focus on capability scaling and suggests that precision and reliability are more important metrics for AI system advancement.
author: George Andrikopoulos

title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
description: New method for diagnosing and fixing capability imbalances in multi-teacher on-policy distillation systems. Addresses challenges in knowledge transfer when teacher models have uneven capabilities across different domains.
author: Huan-ang Gao, Haohan Chi, Yong Yan, Shiyuan Feng, Hanlin Wu, Zheng Jiang, Bingxiang He, Wei-Ying Ma, Ya-Qin Zhang, Hao Zhou

title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
description: Advances in on-policy distillation for long-context reasoning tasks. Introduces group-calibrated approaches that go beyond simple teacher likelihood matching for better knowledge transfer in complex reasoning scenarios.
author: Zhu Zhang, Jixun Wang, Xiaoang Xu, Xiaorong Wang, Zihan Zhou, Zhiyuan Wang, Shuo Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Yuezhi Zhou

title: What is Missing from AI Post-Training: An Empirical Analysis
description: Comprehensive empirical analysis examining what's missing from current AI post-training approaches. Identifies gaps and limitations in post-training methods for large language models.
author: Joy Jia Yin Lim, Xin Huang, Hao Peng, Yaxi Lu, Xin Cong, Zhong Zhang, Maosong Sun, Yankai Lin

title: MLREF: Efficient Module Reuse for Reward Design in Reinforcement Learning via Large Language Models
description: Novel approach using LLMs for efficient module reuse in reward design for reinforcement learning. MLREF leverages large language models to identify and reuse successful reward modules across different RL tasks.
author: Chenglin Liu, Xun Wang, Ruishuo Chen, Zhuoran Li, Longbo Huang

title: To Go Far, Go Together: Diverse Preferences Induce a Curriculum for Reward Optimization
description: Research showing how diverse preferences can induce natural curricula for reward optimization in RL. Demonstrates that incorporating diverse preference data improves reward function learning and agent performance.
author: Taehyung Kim, Jongeun Choi

title: RTPO: Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization for Stabilizing Agentic RL Training
description: New policy optimization method called RTPO (Reverse-Turn Policy Optimization) for stabilizing agentic reinforcement learning training. Addresses instability issues in training AI agents using RL.
author: Yugu Li, Jimmy Cao, Jianglin Qiao, Siyi Hu

title: The Best AI Tools for Developers in 2026 (That I Actually Use)
description: YouTube video reviewing the best AI tools for developers in 2026. Covers tools like Codex, discusses local agentic coding workflows, and running LLMs for development. Provides practical insights on which AI coding tools are most useful in real development scenarios.
author: Unknown YouTube Creator

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast episode #490 featuring Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the comprehensive state of AI in 2026. Covers LLM developments, coding tools, scaling laws, AI agents, GPU availability, China's role in AI, and AGI prospects.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: 8 best AI coding tools for developers: tested & compared!
description: Comprehensive comparison of 8 leading AI coding platforms tested and reviewed by n8n. Covers modern coding tools and development scenarios, providing detailed analysis of AI coding assistants available in 2026.
author: n8n Blog

title: 13 Best AI Coding Tools for Complex Codebases in 2026
description: Focuses on enterprise AI coding tools for complex codebases. Compares tools based on repository-wide indexing, context depth, security controls, and workflow automation capabilities.
author: Augment Code

title: Communications of the ACM - August 2026 Edition
description: ACM's August 2026 issue featuring articles on neural coding and software engineering, exploring AI/ML applications in development. Covers neural coding as software engineering augmentation rather than replacement.
author: Communications of the ACM

title: AI Coding Agents in 2026: Coherence Through Orchestration
description: Analysis of how AI coding agents have matured from autocomplete tools into genuine software producers. Discusses the path to coherent software at scale through better orchestration of AI agents.
author: Mike Mason

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
description: Hacker News discussion about LLM coding workflows and strategies for 2026. Community discussion on balancing human specification versus agent autonomy as a key challenge for AI coding in 2026.
author: Hacker News Community
